correctness.rationale: Zhu's exact occupancy coordinates become, after \(x=1/m\), \(p_{n,k}(x)=S(n,k)x^{n-k}\prod_{j=1}^{k-1}(1-jx)\). Each has degree at most \(n-1\) and a distinct lowest nonzero power \(x^{n-k}\), so the \(n\) coordinate polynomials form a basis of all real polynomials of degree at most \(n-1\). For \(n\ge3\), the quadratic \(-\left(x-1/m_0\right)^2\) is therefore a linear functional of the probability vector and uniquely exposes the finite point \(m_0\) on \(\{0,1,1/2,\ldots\}\); \(-x\) uniquely exposes the limiting point \(m=\infty\). Finally, a point of \(\operatorname{conv}(V_n)\) not itself in \(V_n\) has a finite convex representation involving at least two distinct generators and hence a nontrivial segment decomposition, so it is not extreme.
